questions.question: Describe how the contents page of a school atlas is usually organised.
questions.expected_answer: The contents page is near the front. It lists the sections and maps in the same order as the pages, with a page number for each. It usually starts with how to use the atlas, then world maps, then each continent, then countries and provinces, and ends with statistics, flags and the index.

questions.question: Explain when you would use the index instead of the contents page.
questions.expected_answer: You use the index when you are looking for a particular place, such as a small town, a river or a mountain, and do not know which map it is on. The index at the back lists place names in alphabetical order and gives the page number and grid reference of a map that shows the place.

questions.question: Explain how to use the grid reference C4 to find a place on a map.
questions.expected_answer: Find column C along the top or bottom edge of the map and row 4 along the side. Follow them to the square where they meet. The place will be inside that grid square.
